svg.title: Settlement Claim Recovery Roadmap
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-settlement-claim-roadmap; chapter number: 12; title: Settlement Claim Recovery Roadmap; subtitle: Verify, recover credentials, document honestly, file and confirm; caption: Antitrust and class action money goes only to people who file, and only 4% of eligible consumers do. Each week clears one checkpoint the practitioners flagged.; assumptions note: The weekly sequence organizes the steps practitioners described and is not a deadline any of them stated. Fees come off the top first; about 24% of the $2.8 billion Blue Cross pot goes to plaintiffs' lawyers.; note: Sources are News4JAX The Local Station, Crazy Deals and Steals, Receipts, Horty Springer & Mattern, P.C., The Class Action Attorney and NBC4 Washington.; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Verify the notice; deliverable: Official settlement site confirmed; any upfront payment, gift card, crypto or Social Security number request refused; gate: No payment requested, because real claims carry no administrative charge; week: Week 2; title: Recover claim credentials; deliverable: Unique ID and PIN recovered by searching email for the administrator name, such as Kroll on AT&T, or through the resend page; gate: A working ID and PIN in hand; week: Week 3; title: Build honest counts and proof; deliverable: Fee counts built from old bank statements; Option B Blue Cross filers attach Excel spreadsheets of allowed amounts; gate: Estimates that hold up under penalty of perjury; week: Week 4; title: File with proof and confirm payout; deliverable: Claim filed with uploaded proof toward caps like the $7,500 AT&T ceiling; middleman fees weighed against free filing; gate: Administrator confirms any unexpected check before it is cashed
